clue.text: Inflame family that's led astray

explanation.surface: A family member who has gone off the rails stirs up anger at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to set alight, and figuratively to arouse feelings, just as inflame does.

clue.text: Villain cheated a bit to make slow progress

indicators.note: only a small piece of the phrase is wanted, a run of letters spanning its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A crook who cheated gradually edges forward, bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to inch means to move forward very gradually, a little distance at a time.

clue.text: Issues of a feminine nature

setter's reading: issue means offspring, so these are children who are female

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a phrase about women's concerns; 'issue' in the legal and old sense means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for offspring, and female offspring are a parent's girls.

clue.text: Anger near criminal, for example, being upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top
a criminal version of a word is a bent one, so its letters are corrupted into a new order

e.g. is the standard abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a nearby crook, for instance, and is plainly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger used as a verb, to make someone furious, is a direct synonym of enrage.

clue.text: Lecture when spirit is trapped inside

indicators.note: one thing caught within another sits inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: morale is team spirit or confidence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone delivers a sermon when their courage feels cooped up within them.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise is to preach about right and wrong, which is what lecture means as a verb.

clue.text: Behaving very oddly — furious, like a demo over hair, reportedly

parts.note: mad can mean very angry
as a means like a
a demo, or demonstration, is a protest march

indicators.note: reportedly signals something passed on by word of mouth, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the animal's name is said the same as hair

explanation.surface: A protester is going wild with rage over a march about hairstyles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the march above the next piece. The idiom comes from hares behaving wildly in their spring breeding season.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone acting crazily or eccentrically, as hares were thought to do in spring.

clue.text: Study can make something legible

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
to be able is to be capable of something, i.e. can do it

explanation.surface: Careful study can turn a scrawl into something you can decipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is legible is clear enough to decipher, which is what readable means.

clue.text: Look up racy image, displayed initially for to be shocking

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone searches online for a racy picture, which turns out to be shocking when it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The link 'for to be' is clumsy but simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something sensational or vividly shocking, such as gruesome details or garish images.

clue.text: Excellent boy in charge, when moving at very high speed

parts.note: super is an informal word for excellent
a son is a boy child
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic describes travelling faster than the speed of sound, as Concorde did.

clue.text: Received account for sheets of paper, 500

parts.note: a/c is the abbreviation for account
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives for an order of 500 sheets of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a stationer's measure; twenty of them make a ream, which is the figure the surface hints at with 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquired means obtained or got, the same as received in the sense of coming into possession.

clue.text: Short sailor Rex put out

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
the three letters of put, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as offended, but only 'out' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means brusque or curt in manner, so a short reply is an abrupt one.

clue.text: Had rights and changed a challenging criterion

parts.note: the twelve letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone once held certain rights, but then a tougher test was imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A high standard is a demanding benchmark or level of quality that is hard to meet.

clue.text: Ruling is in trouble, but it's not absolute

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so the two words before it are jumbled

parts.note: a decree is an official ruling
the letters of these two short words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal judgement has run into difficulty, as it is not yet final.
explanation.walkthrough: In English divorce law, a decree nisi was the provisional order, made final by the later decree absolute.
explanation.definitionFit: This provisional divorce order took effect only if no cause was shown otherwise, unlike the final decree absolute.

clue.text: Iron Lawrence found at the fair

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', is known by his initials

explanation.surface: Lawrence is spotted at the fair working the pressing iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event with stalls and games, the kind of village fair held in summer.

clue.text: Model, one playing musical instrument

taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'bad, bad' sounds like emphasis; the first is fodder, the second the instruction. A squib is a small firework that fizzles out if damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is an event that disappoints expectations, like a firework that fails to go off.

clue.text: Benediction not to be sneezed at!

definitions.text: Benediction not to be sneezed at!

parts.note: surface reading: the idiom meaning not to be dismissed or treated as trivial
setter's reading: the blessing said literally to someone who has just sneezed

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not to be sneezed at' means worth having; read literally, it is the phrase said at a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a short blessing, the customary polite response when someone sneezes.

clue.text: Pull the French king from fighter

parts.note: to wrest is to pull something away forcibly

R stands for rex or regina, so for king

explanation.surface: Someone drags the King of France away from a combatant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a combatant in a grappling sport, so a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Parent, one new to Head

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A parent introduces a newcomer to the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Head used as an adjective, as in head office, means chief or principal, the same as main.

clue.text: Hesitation married son deviously hides in discourse

parts.note: the twelve letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a teacher and scholar of Jewish law, often the religious leader of a congregation.

clue.text: Minister to nurse

second meaning: to care for a sick person

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to a clergyman; 'minister to' is the phrasal verb meaning to care for, and the answer takes 'to' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient is to look after them, which matches both nursing and ministering to their needs.
